extracted.intended_audience: general readers, researchers, journalists and policymakers interested in media, disinformation, and Central European politics
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia-style encyclopedic profile of a specific multilingual online news outlet (Visegrád Post), covering its history, funding, editorial orientation, contributors, international links, and criticisms relating to disinformation and extremist ties.

rubrics_metrics.name: State/public funding versus claimed donations
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the portal officially claimed that its operations were funded by reader donations, analyses have proven direct financial support from Hungarian public sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article cites a 2019–2020 grant: Lalma Consulting Hungary Kft. received 4 million forints (~€12,300) from the National Cultural Fund (NKA) allocated from a special ministerial budget. Use of public subsidies despite claims of exclusive donation funding is presented as an indicator of non‑transparent financing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial orientation and source reliance
rubrics_metrics.description: In its reporting on Hungary, Visegrád Post relies almost exclusively on pro-government information sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most frequently cited sources included Mandiner, Magyar Nemzet, the state news agency MTI, and public broadcasters such as M1 and Híradó. Heavy reliance on government or pro-government outlets is flagged as a sign the portal functioned to amplify government narratives to foreign audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideologized content and editorial stance
rubrics_metrics.description: It published heavily ideologized content, including materials attacking LGBT+ communities and the European Union, supporting Viktor Orbán's government, and attacking pro-democratic politicians such as Donald Tusk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include sustained attacks on LGBT+ issues, opposition to COVID-19 vaccination, praise for conservative bishops, and editorial pieces framing geopolitical events to support a pro-government narrative. Such recurring thematic bias is used to characterize the outlet's editorial line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Links to Russian and pro‑Kremlin networks
rubrics_metrics.description: The outlet has faced intense scrutiny over Russian ties, following allegations that it was bankrolled by the Voice of Europe network run by pro‑Kremlin oligarch Viktor Medvedchuk and associated with other pro‑Russian actors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documented partnerships (e.g., TV Libertés), republished interviews with figures like Alexander Dugin, and investigative findings connecting actors in the outlet to Russian influence networks are cited as evidence. Presence of such ties is treated as an indicator of potential disinformation or influence operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connections to far‑right and extremist groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Visegrád Post was linked to Hungarian far‑right Our Homeland Movement, Jobbik (formerly far‑right), neo‑Nazi Pax Hungarica Movement, Russian separatists, and other far‑right organizations across Europe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews, contributor affiliations, event participation, and editorial cooperation with these groups are noted. Associations with extremist actors and groups are presented as a criterion for assessing radicalization and ideological alignment of the outlet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnerships and republishing practices
rubrics_metrics.description: The outlet listed partners such as Magyar Nemzet, Do Rzeczy, Sovereignty.pl, Kurier Plus and the Polish Forum Ekonomiczne and frequently republished partner content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mutual listings as media partners, republishing of interviews and articles from allied outlets, and cooperative event appearances are documented. Heavy cross‑posting with ideologically aligned outlets is shown as a distribution/practice metric that expands reach and reinforces narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media presence and spokesperson activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Founders and key contributors (e.g., Ferenc Almássy, Nicolas de Lamberterie) frequently appeared on pro‑government television channels and other aligned outlets, presenting themselves as experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes Almássy appeared at least 16 times on pro‑government TV and contributed to pro‑government press. Frequent broadcast appearances by outlet figures are used to judge influence and integration into state media ecosystems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of interviews with political figures
rubrics_metrics.description: The outlet conducted interviews with senior representatives and key figures of the ruling Fidesz party and other right‑wing politicians across Central Europe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews with prominent politicians (Orbán, Novák, Varga, Kövér, etc.) and repeated platforming of allied political voices are presented as evidence the portal sought to shape foreign perceptions of Central European politics consistent with government priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media behavior and topical focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Social media presence, particularly on X, heavily focused on Poland and frequently reposted content from specific partner sites; activity slowed in late 2023 and 2024 with final articles mid‑2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patterns such as concentrated country focus, reposting partner content, platform engagement, and abrupt drops or shifts in activity (including domain repurposing in 2025) are treated as operational metrics relevant to assessing reach and lifecycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational transparency and staffing model
rubrics_metrics.description: Almássy said he was editor‑in‑chief and the outlet's only full‑time employee earning €500–600 a month; the site carried no advertising or subscription revenue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Low staffing, absence of traditional revenue streams, and discrepancies between declared funding sources and documented grants are cited as transparency and sustainability indicators that may signal hidden funding or external support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Involvement in conferences and networks linked to influence activities
rubrics_metrics.description: The outlet and its staff participated in regional forums (Forum Ekonomiczne, conferences with foreign speakers) and cooperated with organizations (Ordo Iuris, TV Libertés, Collegium Intermarium) tied to broader conservative and transnational networks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Event participation, organizational partnerships, and shared platforms with actors later identified in investigations (including figures alleged to have ties to Russian influence) are used to map influence pathways and networked dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associations with organizations accused of wrongdoing
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel later worked with or the outlet promoted organizations such as SOS Chrétiens d'Orient, which has been accused of funding pro‑Assad militias and was subject to an anti‑terrorism raid in 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links (employment, contribution, promotion) to organizations under investigation or accused of serious misconduct are highlighted as reputational and risk indicators that affect assessment of the outlet's networks.
